_help: Real-world maximums. whatif.py check FAILs when a number in the table (not marked premise) matches 'unit' and 'meaning' (case-insensitive regex), does not match 'unless', and is above 'max'. Add a limit whenever a review finds an impossible number.

limits.why: the highest air temperature ever measured on Earth is 56.7 °C (Death Valley, 1913, WMO). Only the premise may go higher.
sunlight heats the ground on Earth to at most about 70–75 °C (satellite record, Lut desert).
sunlight at the ground is at most about 1 000–1 100 W/m² (sun overhead, clear sky); 1 361 W/m² is above the atmosphere.
the world record for rain in one day is 1 825 mm (Foc-Foc, Réunion, 1966, WMO).
the record for rain in about an hour is about 305 mm (Holt, Missouri, 1947, WMO).
the strongest wind gust measured (outside tornadoes) is 408 km/h (Barrow Island, 1996, WMO).
the sea is rising about 4–5 mm a year today; more than 10 mm a year is not measured.
all water vapour above a place is at most about 70–80 mm of rain (tropics); about 25 mm on average.
the snowiest season ever measured was about 29 m of fresh snow (Mount Baker, 1998–99).
the fastest human sprint is about 44.7 km/h (Usain Bolt).
